subject: Country-level deployment & availability — EuroTech RFP clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Markovic <elena.markovic@eurotech.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: EuroTech Procurement <procure@eurotech.com>
Date: 2027-02-14 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Country-level deployment & availability — EuroTech RFP clarifications

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks for the initial RFP pack — a few follow-ups from procurement/security as we finish scoring: we need explicit, per-country answers for the following items (EU focus, but please include other regions where relevant):

1) Country availability: List which countries Redwood can guarantee hosted deployment in (i.e., customer data both stored and processed within the country) vs. countries where only regional (e.g., EU) hosting is available. We specifically need Switzerland, Norway, and Ireland called out.

2) Data residency guarantees: Can you commit contractually that customer data (input, output, and logs) will remain in-region/country for each country you claim availability? If there are exceptions (e.g., temporary failover), please describe the conditions and maximum duration.

3) SLA commitments by deployment type (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and whether SLAs vary by country or region. We are interested in uptime %, p95/p99 latency expectations for text generation endpoints (small-medium payloads), and maintenance windows.

4) Audit logs & retention: Can audit logs be restricted to a country? Is long-term archival (7+ years) supported in-region?

5) Key management & encryption: Support for customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM), and confirmation that backups/snapshots are encrypted at rest and in-region.

6) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summary, and any regional certifications (e.g., Swiss-specific controls) — attach redacted evidence where possible.

Please send a consolidated response and a fillable matrix (per-country matrix preferred) by EOD Monday so procurement can finalize scoring. If anything requires legal review, flag it and include an estimated turnaround.

Best,
Elena
---
Elena Markovic
Senior Sourcing Manager, EuroTech Financial
elena.markovic@eurotech.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-02-15 10:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Country-level deployment & availability — EuroTech RFP clarifications

Marissa / Grace — forwarding EuroTech's list below. I drafted a concise approach in the attached spreadsheet (20270214-EuroTech-RFP-clarifications.xlsx) but want to validate the hard constraints before we return the matrix. Proposed workflow:

- Marissa: confirm which countries we can offer country-level hosting (absolute in-country processing/storage) vs EU-region storage only. Call out Switzerland/Norway specifics and any commercial delta for country-grade hosting (dedicated hosts, data centers, or private deployments).
- Grace: confirm audit-log localization capability, long-term archival options (7+ years), and KMS/HSM approaches (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed).
- I will draft the contractor-friendly clause for data locality + fallback conditions and assemble SOC2/pen test redactions.

Quick notes from my side:
- For hosted API (standard shared infrastructure) we generally offer region-level residency (e.g., eu-west-1) but not in-country guarantees except where we run dedicated instances or private deployments.
- Dedicated and Private deployments can be instantiated on customer-requested country zones where we have partners or on-prem capable packages; these carry lead times and commercial adders.
- Fallback: we can support cross-border failover for up to 4 hours for incident mitigation, longer for disaster recovery with explicit contract language. Need legal sign-off on max duration.

I'll leave the technical answers to you both. If we can get a clear matrix back by EOD Tuesday I can send the consolidated response to Elena and attach SOC2 evidence under NDA.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-02-16 08:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Country-level deployment & availability — EuroTech RFP clarifications

Connor / Grace / Elena — attached is a draft country matrix (country-deployment-matrix-2027-02.pdf) with our current posture. Highlights:

- In-country hosting (data processed + stored inside the country) is available today for: Ireland (via eu-west-1 deployments anchored to Dublin), Germany (dedicated pools via partner co-lo), and the UK (where permitted) as a dedicated or private deployment option.
- Switzerland & Norway: we do NOT provide fully hosted, in-country shared infrastructure by default. For those countries we offer two paths:
  - Private deployment (VPC or on-prem package) — full in-country control and residency.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity) placed in nearest certified data center with contractual egress restrictions; physical hosting in-country possible for larger commitments (requires AO and timeline ~8-12 weeks).
- For the rest of the EU (France, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Sweden) we provide region-level residency (data stored/processed in an EU region) but not guaranteed on a per-country islanded basis.

SLA summary (draft):
- Hosted (multi-tenant API): 99.9% availability (monthly), p95 latency target <120ms, p99 <350ms for typical generation loads. Maintenance windows announced 72h in advance for critical infra work.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): 99.95% availability, p95 <80ms, p99 <200ms.
- Private (customer-managed): SLA negotiated with customer; baseline targets similar to dedicated when Redwood manages runtime.

Audit logs & retention:
- We can retain audit logs in-region for customers on Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted customers can elect region-level retention (EU) but per-country archival depends on hosting topology. Long-term archival (7+ years) feasible via customer-configured exports to an in-country storage bucket (customer or partner-managed).

KMS/Encryption:
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK) supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted customers, BYOK is supported for data-at-rest where KMS integrations are available; otherwise we use Redwood-managed KMS with strict separation. All traffic TLS 1.2+ in transit; at-rest encryption AES-256. Backups inherit same encryption and residency rules as primary storage.

Evidence: SOC 2 Type II is available (redacted), and we can provide a penetration test summary under NDA. We do not currently hold Switzerland-specific regulatory attestations but can provide control mappings and partner evidence on request.

Attachments: country-deployment-matrix-2027-02.pdf (draft), and a row-by-row workbook in the .xlsx.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Elena Markovic <elena.markovic@eurotech.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-17 14:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Country-level deployment & availability — EuroTech RFP clarifications

Thanks Marissa — that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications from security/procurement before we score:

1) Singapore & APAC: EuroTech has a small operation in Singapore. Can Redwood confirm whether country-level hosting or Private/Dedicated options are available in Singapore, and any minimum commit required?
2) Logs retention: Our legal team insists on the ability to keep audit logs in-country for 7 years for specific regulated lines of business. Can you confirm an operational pattern (automated export to customer-controlled bucket, or Redwood managed archival) and whether that export can be performed without any cross-border transfer during the export process?
3) Data subject requests (GDPR): please confirm the point of contact and the SLA you propose for fulfilling DSARs (e.g., 30 days standard, expedited options).
4) Evidence: Please attach the redacted SOC 2 Type II and indicate whether you will provide a signed letter confirming no cross-border transfer during archival, subject to contract.

If you can include the above in your consolidated reply, procurement will finalize vendor scoring.

Best,
Elena
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Markovic <elena.markovic@eurotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-18 16:40:00 -05:00
Subject: Final consolidated response — EuroTech RFP (country availability + evidence)

Elena — thanks for the follow-ups. Please find our consolidated answers below and attached artifacts (country-deployment-matrix-2027-02.pdf, 20270214-EuroTech-RFP-clarifications.xlsx, redwood-soc2-type2-redacted.pdf). Summary: 

- Singapore/APAC: Country-level hosting in Singapore is available via a Private or Dedicated deployment through our APAC partner. Minimum lead time is 6–10 weeks and typically requires a multi-month reserved capacity commitment for dedicated hosting. For small teams, Private (customer-managed VPC) is the recommended path.

- Logs retention (7+ years): For Dedicated and Private customers we support in-country archival using an automated export pipeline to a customer-controlled storage bucket (S3/GCS-equivalent provided by partner) located in the requested country. The export process can be configured so that no data leaves the country during transfer; we will include contractual language and operational runbook in the SOW. For hosted multi-tenant customers, per-country archival is not available by default — we recommend dedicated/private for regulated archival requirements.

- DSARs / GDPR: Standard DSAR SLA is 30 days. We offer an expedited path (10 business days) for critical regulated requests subject to an agreed process and potential additional fees. Point of contact for DSAR intake: privacy@redwood.com; for legal escalation please contact legal@redwood.com.

- Evidence & contractual commitments: Attached is a redacted SOC 2 Type II report. We will provide a contractual attestation that archival exports configured as in-country will not be routed outside the country during the export process; we will need the final SOW and an NDA to supply the unredacted SOC and penetration test artifacts.

- Fallback / failover: we propose maximum automated failover duration of 4 hours (incident mitigation) without cross-border data transfer for customer-sensitive workloads; DR over longer windows can be arranged with explicit contractual exception and notification.

Next steps: Connor to produce proposed contractual wording for the data locality + archival clause and deliver a final matrix by Thursday COB. Marissa to provide the partner contact for Switzerland/Norway country hosting and an estimated TTM/cost delta for in-country dedicated hosting. Grace to finalize the KMS/HSM options and a short runbook for archival exports.

If helpful, I'm available for a 30-minute executive call with your security and procurement teams tomorrow morning.

Best regards,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
